title: Oboe
summary: Limits first: the reed is assembled, not measured; its mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed. Since the reed's closure stop (a857c6f17) the scale sits -7 to +33 c from equal temperament (F4 at its printed pressure only); before it, 22 to 158 c flat. At the pages' 7.4 kPa F4 plays an octave up (677 Hz). The old flat scale was the reed passing through its lay. The tongue is a labelled borrowed-number row (`tongue_contact`, described near the end) on the Bb4, F4, D5 and Ab5 pages and is not on the Db4, G5 and D4 pages (the D4 page, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, carries none; the tongue was tried there, below); only the first open hole has a nonlinear loss, a quasi-steady orifice (all eleven open holes on the D5 page, `open_hole_orifice 11`, all five on the F4 page, `open_hole_orifice 5`, and all nine on the Ab5 page, `open_hole_orifice 9`; all three on the D4 page, whose discontinuous-Galerkin card carries `dg_terminal_orifice 0.61` on its three open chimneys; the Db4 page, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, has no orifice law at all), and the breath noise row on Bb4, Db4, D4, F4, D5, G5 and Ab5 drives only 10 to 20 kHz on this reed's 0.87 mm duct. A C major scale and Ode to Joy are up, each note its own render at the pages' 7.4 kPa except F4, at its printed 6865 Pa, on fingerings inferred from Table III of Nederveen and de Bruijn 1967, the one complete oboe tone-hole table this project holds. Bb4 (6 of 15, strict 5, with the contraction, profile, interaction and length rows below) is a graded page re-rendered after the stop, Db4 (6 of 14, strict 4, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore at its converged 20 kHz band, observed to 9.6 kHz, below) is a graded page, and Bb4 sounds as B4, 102 c sharp of its name; G5 sounds at its written octave (790.90 Hz, G5 +15.2 c) on a card with a re-specified octave vent, and has no grade; Ab5 sounds at its written octave as a single series (819.53 Hz, Ab5 -23.3 c) on a card with a re-specified octave vent, and has no grade and no count (below); D4, F4 and D5 are first pages at their printed pressures. A staple pressure recovery row (Almeida, Vergez and Caussé 2007; C_P 0.8 and S_c 4 mm^2, one measured reed's two numbers, borrowed; commit b57b46619) is on the D4 and D5 pages: D4, which does not speak at 6178 Pa without it, speaks with it (301.95 Hz, 48 c sharp of D4, on the first staple page; ungraded, a listening page). The D5 page also carries the clarinet's bore air temperature profile (Noreland 2013, measured on a clarinet and borrowed for the oboe, positions rescaled), the mutual radiation impedance of the open holes and the bell, the printed thick-wall hole lengths of Lefebvre and Scavone, and, as a labelled bound trial, a jet contraction row (`contraction 0.611`, the two-dimensional free-streamline bound pi/(pi+2); commit 25b9bc64c): no double-reed value is printed; the card's reed area (2.0 mm^2) is Almeida's printed typical oboe rest area, not their fitted 3.05 to 3.37 mm^2, so the reed they measured passes more flow than the card's (peak 249 to 313 mL/s against 132, and 81 with the row), 0.611 is a borrowed value and not a coefficient of this reed; the channel's unsteady inertance has no printed effective length and is not in the row. With those five rows the page sounded at 578.17 Hz, D5 -27.2 c (from -73.1 c without any of them, and 571.12 Hz, -48.5 c, with the first four), and scored 5 of 14, 3 on the strict ruler, against 4 and 3 for the page without the contraction row: the row brought the spectral flux inside the loose ruler, while the spectral distance, the third-octave envelope, the harmonic levels, the wavelet and cepstral gaps, odd against even and the centroid all widened, and the page was 5.1 dB quieter (96.5 dB SPL against 101.6). The D5 page now carries `open_hole_orifice 11` (commit 43ad828c9; it carried `open_hole_orifice 3` from commit 043f9b8e9 until then): the quasi-steady orifice loss of all eleven open holes (158 to 539 mm from the reed) solved together through the bore, each hole's coefficient from the gas at that hole, with two stated approximations: each orifice sees its own uncoupled radiation load, not the coupled one of the interaction row, and the sound the holes radiate still comes from the linear network, as for the first hole alone; the fully coupled orifice network is not built. With the loss on the first three holes the page sounded at 579.51 Hz, D5 -23.2 c, and scored 6 of 14, 5 on the strict ruler, against 5 and 3 for the page without the orifice row: the pitch came inside both rulers and the spectral flux inside the strict one, the waveform locked slightly less (autocorrelation 0.992 against 1.000), and the page was 0.3 dB quieter (96.2 dB SPL against 96.5); the render took 2.2 times the CPU. Three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so the cap is now twelve and the row takes every open hole: on all eleven the page sounds at 579.77 Hz, D5 -22.4 c, the level and the harmonic levels H1 to H8 are the same to the digit shown (96.2 dB SPL), and the count stays 6 of 14, 5 on the strict ruler, with seven gaps to the recording slightly larger (harmonics-to-noise 1.04 to 1.20 dB, spectral flux 0.78 to 0.92 dB, centroid, spectral distance, envelope, harmonic levels, STFT) and four slightly smaller (wavelet, cepstral envelope, pitch, odd against even); the render takes 1118 s of CPU against 591 s for the three-hole page, far less than the growth of the realized kernels (15 to 143) would give. The same card without the staple row scored 5 of 14, so on D5 the staple row costs one measure (spectral flux) and brings the pitch 15 c nearer the recording. The staple row lowered the count on Db4 (3 to 2) and Bb4 (6 to 5), so those pages stay without it. The contraction row (0.611, the same bound trial as on D5, on the live card with no other row) raised the Db4 count from 3 to 4 of 14 and the strict count stayed at 3: that page sounded at 280.73 Hz, 22.0 c sharp of Db4 and 33.1 c sharp of the recording (the page without the row, 275.08 Hz, was 2.0 c from the recording), so the pitch measure was lost from both rulers and odd against even from the strict one, while the partial frequencies and the attack came inside both rulers and the harmonics-to-noise reading flipped from 27.6 dB below the recording to 14.0 dB above it; the page was 4.8 dB quieter (97.8 dB SPL against 102.6) and the spectral, envelope, harmonic-level and wavelet gaps widened slightly. With `open_hole_orifice 3` as well (the card's only three open holes, 463, 499 and 539 mm from the reed, solved together, with the two approximations named on D5) that page kept 4 of 14, strict 3, at 280.80 Hz, +22.4 c from Db4 and 33.5 c sharp of the recording, 97.7 dB SPL: the row moved almost nothing on this note, and the cause is not known. The transfer-matrix Db4 page (replaced since by the discontinuous-Galerkin page described after it) carried the contraction row with the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths, and not the orifice row: it sounded at 274.99 Hz, 13.8 c flat of Db4 and 2.7 c flat of the recording, and scored 6 of 14, strict 6, against 4 and 3 for the page it replaced (and 3 and 3 for the original page): pitch, odd against even and harmonics-to-noise (41.4 dB against the recording's 40.4) came inside both rulers, while the cepstral envelope, partial trajectory, partial frequency and spectral flux moved slightly farther, and the page was 1.0 dB quieter (96.7 dB SPL against 97.7). The orifice row put on top of those four rows lowered it to 5 of 14, strict 5 (the harmonics-to-noise gap went from 0.92 to 2.81 dB and left both rulers; the cepstral envelope, 15.37 to 16.46 dB, and odd against even, 0.05 to 0.32 dB, were worse and stayed inside; the pitch, 2.69 to 2.59 c, and the level, 96.65 to 96.67 dB SPL, did not move; the render took 1884 s of CPU against 778), so the orifice row stayed off that page, the one oboe page that dropped it from its posted card. The Db4 page was, until the converged bore described after this paragraph, the discontinuous-Galerkin render at the 9.6 kHz design band (degree 2, 51 elements, wall memory to 9.6 kHz, the twenty chimneys as ducts, a sparse Krylov propagator, the reed as one lumped mode on a penalty contact, the bell and open holes as one computed baffled-piston array, the contraction row and the clarinet's air profile, no printed hole lengths, no orifice): it sounds at 276.58 Hz, 3.8 c flat of Db4 and 7.4 c sharp of the recording (the page it replaces: 2.7 c flat), steady to 0.0 c, 93.2 dB SPL (3.4 dB below), and scores 7 of 14, strict 4, against 6 and 6: spectral distance (26.05 to 12.68 dB) and harmonic levels (15.80 to 9.36 dB) come inside the loose ruler and harmonics-to-noise leaves it, and on the strict ruler odd against even and harmonics-to-noise leave, so the strict count falls from 6 to 4 while the loose count rises by one. It is too clean: harmonics-to-noise 63.4 dB against the recording's 40.4 (the page it replaces read 41.4). The pitch gap grows from 2.69 to 7.38 c, odd against even from 0.05 to 5.90 dB, the partial trajectory from 11.53 to 14.81 dB, the attack from 1.61 to 1.95 (log2) and the spectral flux from 2.04 to 2.25 dB, while the third-octave envelope (20.71 to 8.55 dB), the cepstral envelope (15.37 to 7.98), the wavelet (23.48 to 17.42) and STFT (30.66 to 26.43) gaps and the centroid (13.82 to 8.41 st) shrink; the render takes 11862 s of CPU on ts2. It posts by the loose count, with the strict fall and the too-clean note named on its page. The Db4 page now is the same card on the converged bore: only the `dg_bore` header changed, the degree of the elements 2 to 3, the wall poles 48 to 60, the band edge 9.6 to 20 kHz, the DOF cap 20480 to 32768 and the wall quadrature 3 to 4, observed to 9.6 kHz as before (the band edge did not matter: a 14 kHz bore pilot renders the 20 kHz bore's waveform to one 16-bit step; the other four changed together and were not isolated, so which of them moved the band energy is not shown). The 9.6 kHz bore was not converged: on the converged bore the same note holds 7.8 dB more energy in 1.5 to 4.8 kHz and 7.2 dB more in 4.8 to 9.6 kHz (steady 1 to 2 s, re total: -22.23 and -29.18 dB on the 9.6 kHz bore, -14.43 and -21.99 dB on the converged one; the recording -8.95 and -41.25 dB). It sounds at 276.57 Hz, Db4 -3.8 c and 7.3 c sharp of the recording (the 9.6 kHz bore 276.59 Hz), at 93.4 dB SPL (peak 3.38 Pa), and scores 6 of 14, strict 4, on lib1, the library that reproduces the live pair (lib0139 reads the 9.6 kHz bore 8 of 14, strict 5, and this render 6 and 4): the loose count falls by one because the spectral distance leaves the loose ruler (12.68 to 15.73 dB), and the strict count is unchanged, the same four measures inside. Gaps to the recording that grow: spectral distance 12.68 to 15.73 dB, third-octave envelope 8.55 to 11.27, harmonic levels 9.36 to 10.98, STFT 26.43 to 28.94, wavelet 17.42 to 19.57, partial frequency 0.29 to 0.39 c, and by under 0.05 the cepstral envelope, odd against even and partial trajectory; gaps that shrink: harmonics-to-noise 22.94 to 16.10 dB (the note reads 56.5 dB clean against the recording's 40.4, still too clean), centroid 8.41 to 6.26 st and spectral flux 2.25 to 2.04. The 4.8 to 9.6 kHz band now holds 19.3 dB more energy than the recording's, where the 9.6 kHz bore held 12.1 dB more, and the 1.5 to 4.8 kHz band is 5.5 dB under the recording's, where it was 13.3 dB under. The render took 33 554 s of CPU on K9 (11 862 s on the 9.6 kHz bore, on an earlier binary). It posts as the resolution fix it is, the 9.6 kHz bore not being converged, and not by its count. The Bb4 page first carried three of those groups without the staple row: the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes (the doubled hole, holes 8 and 9 at one axial station, is coupled at its touching distance since commit 418a8f86b; before it the engine refused) and the printed hole lengths. It scored 6 of 15 against 6, a tie on the loose ruler, and 4 against 5 on the strict ruler (spectral flux left it), sounded 8.8 c sharper (496.22 Hz) and 0.87 dB quieter, and eight gaps to the recording moved slightly farther, against hundredths gained; with the staple row added it fell to 5 of 15. The Bb4 page now carries the contraction row as well (0.611, borrowed, a bound trial, no staple row, no orifice row): it sounds at 494.45 Hz, 102.0 c sharp of Bb4 and 99.6 c sharp of the recording, and scores 6 of 15, strict 5, against 6 and 4 for the page it replaces and 6 and 5 for the original page: spectral flux comes back inside the strict ruler, while the spectral distance, third-octave envelope, harmonic levels, cepstral envelope, odd against even and centroid move slightly farther, and the STFT and wavelet gaps, the pitch gap (105.8 to 99.6 c), harmonics-to-noise and attack move nearer; the page is 4.0 dB quieter (99.6 dB SPL against 103.6). On the original card the contraction row alone lowered the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4); together with the three groups it ties the loose count and gains a strict measure, so it is on the Bb4 page. The orifice row (`open_hole_orifice 3`, which solves the doubled hole with its neighbour) on the live Bb4 card lowered the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4; spectral flux leaves both rulers). Put on top of the four-row Bb4 page it lowers the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4; spectral flux leaves both rulers, 0.95 to 1.28 dB), moves the pitch 13.4 c lower and the level 1.03 dB lower, and takes 498 s of CPU against 222, so the orifice row stays off Bb4, as on Db4. On F4 the staple row alone moved the register edge below the printed pressure (676 Hz, the second register, at 6865 Pa), so the staple row alone stays off F4. The contraction row alone (0.611, on the live card with no other row) keeps F4 in the first register at its printed 6865 Pa and raises the count from 5 to 6 of 15, strict 5 to 6: that page sounded at 352.49 Hz, F4 +16.1 c (the page without the row, 350.37 Hz, +5.7 c), gained the cepstral envelope and the harmonics-to-noise gap (11.5 to 5.7 dB) inside both rulers and lost spectral flux from both, while the pitch gap widened from 5.8 to 16.3 c, the partial-trajectory and attack gaps widened, and the page was 3.3 dB quieter (98.0 dB SPL against 101.3). With `open_hole_orifice 3` as well (the card's first three open holes, 351, 365 and 431 mm from the reed, solved together, with the two approximations named on D5) that page kept 6 of 15, strict 6, at 352.52 Hz, F4 +16.2 c, 97.8 dB SPL: the row moved almost nothing on this note, and the cause is not known. The F4 page now also carries the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths: it sounds at 354.18 Hz, F4 +24.4 c, and scores 6 of 15, strict 6, level with the page it replaces (no measure changes side of either ruler; the original page was 5 and 5): the pitch gap grows from 16.4 to 24.5 c, the spectral distance, third-octave envelope, STFT, partial trajectory, harmonics-to-noise, attack and spectral flux move slightly farther, the harmonic levels, wavelet, cepstral envelope and centroid slightly nearer, and the page is 0.6 dB quieter (97.2 dB SPL against 97.8); the render takes 990 s of CPU against 421 for the page without the orifice row. The F4 page now carries `open_hole_orifice 5` (commit 43ad828c9; it carried `open_hole_orifice 3` from commit 043f9b8e9 until then): the same orifice loss on all five open holes (351 to 539 mm from the reed), solved together; three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so this is a consistency fix. It sounds at 354.19 Hz, F4 +24.4 c, 97.2 dB SPL, and scores 6 of 15, strict 6, level with the three-hole page (no measure changes side of either ruler): the tone moves by 0.05 c, and the level and the harmonic levels H1 to H8 are the same to the digit shown. Four gaps to the recording grew slightly (partial trajectory 19.76 to 19.99 dB, pitch 24.55 to 24.59 c, harmonics-to-noise 6.92 to 6.93 dB, spectral flux 2.36 to 2.39 dB) and four shrank (cepstral envelope, partial frequency, odd against even, centroid); the render takes 1072 s of CPU against 935 s for the three-hole page on the same build. With the staple row and the contraction row together the note also stays in the first register (353.23 Hz) and scores 5 of 15, strict 5, level with the page without them. Ab5 is posted at its written octave with the contraction row (0.611, the bound trial of the D5 page; no staple row), the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes, the printed hole lengths, `open_hole_orifice 9` (all nine open holes, 129 to 539 mm from the reed; until commit 43ad828c9 the page carried `open_hole_orifice 3`, the vent and holes 11 and 12, because three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so the nine-hole row is a consistency fix), the tongue row `tongue_contact` (described near the end) and the octave vent, hole 2, re-specified to a bore of 0.81 mm and a height of 0.7 mm, the same vent as the G5 page (its numbers and sources are in the G5 paragraph; the old 6 mm height was an assumption copied from hole 3, and the depth stands on the repo's citation of a maker's page only). With that vent it sounds at 819.53 Hz, Ab5 -23.3 c and 30.5 c flat of the recording's 834.08 Hz, a single steady series (the strongest line holds the pitch to 0.00 c across 0.3 to 2.3 s; autocorrelation at the pitch's own period 0.970 with the period moving 2.3 c, at the doubled period 0.997), at 100.8 dB SPL (peak 6.45 Pa), and the clip no longer falls back to the first register at its end (the last strong line is 816 Hz); harmonics-to-noise reads 49.3 dB against the recording's 43.0. With the old 0.3 mm by 6 mm vent the same card sounded at 817.20 Hz, Ab5 -28.2 c and 35.4 c flat of the recording, as a period doubling and not a clean note: the line at half the frequency, 408.69 Hz, stood 25.3 dB under the pitch line (autocorrelation at the pitch's own period 0.461 with the period moving 174 c; at the doubled period 0.957 and 0.5 c), at 99.2 dB SPL, with the last 0.15 s falling back toward 411 Hz as the blowing pressure released; the page before it (the card with the vent and the closure stop and none of these rows) sounded an octave down at 411.32 Hz, Ab4 -16.7 c, and the three-hole page sounded at 817.12 Hz, also period-doubled. Without the orifice row the note is not clean either (lines at 835.7, 1262.3, 1671.4, 2489.1 and 2507.1 Hz within 5 dB of each other; autocorrelation 0.877 at 417.84 Hz with the period moving 37 c); that was read with the old vent and not repeated with the new one. Ab5 has no ruler, so there is no grade and no count: its tests are the register against the written note, whether it speaks and locks, and the level; correcting the vent's assumed height removes the period doubling and the fall back, and the clip is 1.6 dB louder (peak 6.45 Pa against 5.40). G5 is posted at its written octave, on the `g4c` card (the contraction row, the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths) with the octave vent, hole 2, re-specified from the printed 0.3 mm bore and the assumed 6 mm height to a bore of 0.81 mm and a height of 0.7 mm: it sounds at 790.90 Hz, G5 +15.2 c and 12.7 c sharp of the recording's 785.13 Hz, a single steady series (autocorrelation 0.981 with the period moving 2.2 c, the strongest line holding to 0.03 c), at 100.8 dB SPL (peak 6.86 Pa), where the page it replaces sounded an octave down at 398.35 Hz (autocorrelation 0.956 with the period moving 0.8 c; 103.4 dB SPL, peak 12.24 Pa). The same card with the old vent is not a note: two tones 15.3 Hz apart at 387.4 and 402.7 Hz (G4 -20 c and +45 c) with their second harmonics, the strongest line jumping between about 1193 and 2364 Hz from one 100 ms slice to the next, autocorrelation 0.907 with the period moving 40 c; with `open_hole_orifice 3` as well the strongest line holds 783.4 Hz (the written G5) in every slice, but the waveform does not repeat at that frequency (autocorrelation 0.327) and repeats near 394 Hz, an octave down, with autocorrelation 0.743 and the period moving 31 c; so the old vent never reached the written octave. The vent's numbers, as they stand: the bore range 0.66 to 0.81 mm is the patent's print (US 6,124,537); the depth 0.7 mm and the ranges 0.5 to 0.7 mm (bore) and 0.25 to 0.7 mm (depth) are S. Fox's maker's page as the repo's notes cite it, and stand on that citation only, because the page could not be retrieved; the old 6 mm height was an assumption copied from hole 3, and the old 0.3 mm bore is Table III's printed but doubtful value. The point (0.405 mm radius, 0.7 mm height) was declared before any render, and the page posts because all three corners of the sourced range reach the written octave: 792.57 Hz (radius 0.25 mm, height 0.25 mm), 791.75 Hz (0.35 mm, 0.7 mm) and 790.92 Hz (0.405 mm, 0.7 mm), the pitch falling 1.7 c per step as the vent opens. Hand arithmetic, not the engine's law, puts the old vent at 42 to 57 times the bore's characteristic impedance at its station, an almost closed hole, and the three sourced vents at 0.65 to 1.7 times. The Woodwind Fingering Guide's chart gives G5 as G4's fingering plus the first (thumb) octave key; which of holes 1, 2 and 5 that key opens is not printed, and hole 2 was chosen by position (a semi-automatic oboe lets the thumb key work either vent). Harmonics-to-noise reads 49.2 dB against the old page's 57.4 (the recording 36.5) and spectral flux 3.45 dB against 2.88 (the recording 2.42). G5 has no ruler, so there is no grade and no count. The paragraph from here to the one on the converged bore describes the earlier D4 page, on the reed-performance route, which the converged-bore page replaces; it carried, besides its staple row, the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes, the printed hole lengths and `open_hole_orifice 3` (all three of its open holes, 431, 499 and 539 mm from the reed) and the tongue row `tongue_contact` (described near the end), and not the contraction row: added to the staple, profile, interaction and length rows it silences D4 at 6178 Pa, with or without the orifice row (peak 0.03 Pa, lock 0.13), so it stays off D4. The D4 page sounds at 303.78 Hz, more than 50 c sharp of D4 and so nearer Eb4 than D4 (the page it replaces, 301.96 Hz, sat 48 c sharp of D4), steady (autocorrelation 1.000, the period moving 0.1 c), at 101.4 dB SPL, 0.81 dB under the page it replaces (102.2 dB SPL). Its pitch gap to the recording (294.04 Hz) grows from 46.02 to 56.46 c: 10.1 c of the 10.4 c step comes from the profile, interaction and length rows and 0.3 c from the orifice row, which also costs 911 s of CPU against 369 without it and 116 for the page it replaces. D4 has no ruler, so there is no count and no grade, and the page is a listening page. The gaps to the recording that grow, from regrade.py on lib0139: pitch, spectral distance (32.17 to 32.93 dB), third-octave envelope (22.67 to 23.47), harmonic levels (22.84 to 23.10), STFT (38.62 to 38.98), spectral flux (1.02 to 1.44) and harmonics-to-noise (6.35 to 13.03 dB: the page reads 55.3 dB against the recording's 42.3, 13 dB too clean, and about 7 dB of that rise comes from the orifice row, cause not known); the wavelet, cepstral envelope, odd against even, attack and centroid gaps shrink slightly, and partial trajectory and partial frequency do not move. The rows on Ab5 and D4 were rendered together, so what each does alone was not measured there. The D4 page now is the discontinuous-Galerkin render on the converged 14 kHz bore, with no tongue row: the card of the 9.6 kHz trial (`oboe-d4-b9k6-full-all-ta`) with only its `dg_bore` header changed (the degree of the elements, the wall poles, the band edge, the DOF cap and the wall quadrature, `51 3 60 50 14000 0.01 1e-11 32768 4`), rendered on K10 in 30 834 s of CPU, and it replaces the reed-performance D4 page described above. It sounds at 292.00 Hz, D4 -9.9 c and 12.1 c flat of the recording (the earlier page 303.78 Hz, 58.6 c sharp), at 94.88 dB SPL (the earlier page 101.37), and its pitch gap is 12.03 c against 56.46. D4 still has no ruler, so there is no count and no grade; of the gaps to the recording 11 shrink (spectral distance 32.93 to 18.87 dB, third-octave envelope 23.47 to 14.20, harmonic levels 23.10 to 12.42, STFT 39.04 to 30.69, wavelet 26.18 to 19.84, cepstral envelope 12.91 to 7.75, pitch, centroid 17.57 to 2.34 st, odd against even 4.83 to 3.32, harmonics-to-noise 13.02 to 12.10, attack 2.64 to 2.19) and 3 grow (spectral flux 1.31 to 2.01, partial trajectory 13.99 to 14.01, partial frequency 0.57 to 0.59). The tongue was tried on this bore (the typed reed's `tongue_contact`, commit 6e6d88fdf, 28 134 s of wall time): the steady tone is unchanged and the time to half of the steady level falls from 241.4 to 215.0 ms, but the render sounds before the blow starts (0.114 Pa rms in its first 10 ms, nothing by 70 ms), because the tongue's first load, about 0.6 N, is applied at the first sample to a reed at its rest opening, and its partial-trajectory gap rises from 14.01 to 34.51 dB; the page therefore carries no tongue, and the tongue page waits for a start state in which the reed begins at its equilibrium under the tongue. The tongue is the opt-in `tongue_contact` row (commit d986948c3; Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2009, Eq. 6, the clamped-free cantilever mode's projection of a uniform contact strip at the reed tip) on the Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and D4 pages: `tongue_contact 1.12e-5 6.979e-5 0.2 0.1845 0.005`, a pad of 2 mm by this reed's 5.6 mm (2 mm by 13 mm is Li 2016's contact for a clarinet reed, kept in length and set to this reed's width) pressing the reed tip with 0.2 N until 0.1845 s and letting go over 5 ms. The effective area, 6.979e-5 m^2, is this reed's own face, k h0 / pM, fixed by the card's reed row and not borrowed; the 2 mm length, the 0.2 N and the 5 ms (Almeida 2017) are the clarinet's, and 0.1845 s is the blow's 0.15 s start plus 34.5 ms, the alto saxophone tonguing contact time of Hofmann 2012. No oboe tongue is printed, and the 0.2 N is below the 1.24 N that this reed's stiffness takes at its 0.357 mm opening, so by that arithmetic the tongue alone does not close the reed; the render's reed-opening trace was not read. On every one of the five pages the steady tone is untouched (pitch within 0.03 c, level within 0.005 dB, centroid within 0.1 %, harmonics to the digit shown) and the rise comes earlier: the time to half of the steady level falls from 241 to 228 ms on Bb4, 428 to 371 ms on F4, 216 to 210 ms on D5, 200 to 193 ms on Ab5 and 290 to 261 ms on D4, and the waveform parts from the render without the row at 175 to 197 ms and is not phase-locked back afterwards. Bb4, F4 and D5 tie their counts (6 of 15, strict 5; 6 of 15, strict 6; 6 of the 14 with a ruler, strict 5; the same measures inside): the attack gap grows on Bb4 (3.21 to 3.41, log2) and D5 (5.11 to 5.15), whose recordings attack slowly (163 and 259 ms), and shrinks on F4 (2.80 to 2.35; 98 to 71 ms against 14), where the partial-trajectory gap also shrinks (19.99 to 15.96 dB). The build of these pages, K10, is not byte-equal to the earlier pages' clips: the same cards without the row differ from them by -49 to -67 dB re signal after 0.2 to 0.4 s, and on Bb4 part of the grader's change (partial trajectory 10.41 to 13.52 dB, wavelet 31.08 to 31.97, STFT 42.99 to 43.16) is the build and not the tongue. The Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and D4 paragraphs above describe those pages before the tongue row; their steady numbers still hold, except F4's, which the lay moved (next paragraph). Ab5 (a period doubling at 817.20 Hz with the old vent and the half-pitch line 25.3 dB under; the peak falls from 5.86 to 5.40 Pa and the lock at the pitch's own period goes from 0.459 to 0.461; with the re-specified vent the doubling is gone, see the Ab5 paragraph) and D4 (303.78 Hz, 101.4 dB SPL; the gaps to the recording that grow are STFT 38.98 to 39.04, cepstral envelope 12.61 to 12.91, attack 2.43 to 2.64 and centroid 17.52 to 17.57, and spectral flux shrinks 1.44 to 1.31) have no ruler and no count. G5 has no tongue page: the card tried (the contraction card, `g4c`, with the old vent) does not hold one series with or without the row: the spectrum stands on two tones 15.3 Hz apart at 387.4 and 402.7 Hz (G4 -20 c and +45 c, the first register, an octave below the written note) with their second harmonics and a product line near 790 Hz, and the strongest line jumps between slices (autocorrelation 0.907, the period moving 40 c); the row makes the rise 7 ms earlier and changes none of that. The same row with the effective area scaled with the strip (3.278e-5 m^2, modal factor 0.816) was also rendered on Bb4, F4 and D5 and moved the attack the same way and the tone not at all; it is not posted. The measured reed lay (the four optional lay fields of the `reed` row, `reed 0.000357 0.0056 17720 2.2e-5 3464 0.114 5.7437e6 2.0 1.6e-4 0.0`) is on the F4 page: the stiffness 5.7437e6 is Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012 Table 1's printed clarinet contact stiffness per area, 8.23e10, times this reed's own face, 6.979e-5 m^2; the exponent 2.0, the onset opening 1.6e-4 m (45 % of this reed's 0.357 mm rest opening) and the Hunt-Crossley loss 0.0 are the clarinet pages' values, borrowed; no oboe lay is printed. Tried on top of the tongue row on Bb4, F4 and D5, it raised the pitch on all three (Bb4 494.45 to 497.11 Hz, +9.3 c; F4 354.19 to 356.28 Hz, +10.2 c; D5 579.77 to 589.25 Hz, +28.1 c, as the grader reads them). On F4 it ties the count, 6 of 15 and strict 6 with the same measures inside, so the page posts with it: it sounds at 356.28 Hz, F4 +34.6 c and 34.8 c sharp of the recording (the pitch gap 24.59 to 34.79 c), at 97.7 dB SPL (peak 6.11 Pa, 0.4 dB louder), the harmonics-to-noise gap grows from 6.94 to 7.99 dB, STFT from 40.30 to 41.26, partial trajectory from 15.96 to 16.66 and attack from 2.35 to 2.43, while the centroid (14.88 to 13.81 st), odd against even (6.88 to 5.96), spectral distance, envelope, harmonic levels, wavelet, cepstral and spectral-flux gaps shrink; the lock is 0.984 against 0.950. On Bb4 it was tried and is not posted: the loose count holds (6 of 15) and the strict count falls from 5 to 4 (spectral flux leaves the strict ruler, 0.95 to 1.11 dB), and the pitch gap grows from 99.58 to 108.87 c. On D5 it was tried and is not posted: the count falls from 6 to 5 of 14 and from 5 to 4 on the strict ruler (spectral flux leaves both rulers, 0.79 to 1.35 dB, and the harmonics-to-noise gap grows from 1.46 to 5.03 dB), and the pitch, 12.5 c flat of the recording before, is 15.6 c sharp of it after. The render's reed-opening trace was not read, so why the row lifts the pitch is not shown. The reed channel's viscous slit (`slit_length 0.025`; 25 mm is the clarinet pages' slit length, borrowed as a substitute because no oboe channel length is printed) was tried on the D4 card, which has the staple row and no contraction row (the slit law refuses the contraction): it renders to the end and the note jumps to the second register, 583.5 Hz, D5 -11.4 c, where the card without the row sounds at 303.78 Hz in the first; the series stands on 583.5 Hz (the lines at the odd multiples of 291.75 Hz are 80 to 110 dB under the strongest line, the second harmonic at 1167 Hz), the level is 1.01 Pa rms against 2.34 Pa (7.3 dB quieter) and the peak 5.33 Pa against 13.86 Pa, and the grader refuses the clip as not the named note (the D4 fundamental, 293.7 Hz, is 63 dB under the strongest line). It is not posted, and the slit length was not tuned, since any other length would be an invented one. Eb6 has no render because the printed ladder ends at D5.
physics_present: generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches and a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet; a description gives them this bore and a reed with values partly borrowed from the clarinet, and the posted first renders come from it

flow noise at the reed on Bb4, Db4, D4, F4, D5, G5 and Ab5 (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, extrapolated), with the card's first bore record, 0.87 mm, as its duct radius, by the clarinet cards' rule. At that radius it drives only 10 to 20 kHz, and the code takes the open-area ratio as 0 where this reed's is about 0.8
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two professional oboe players are retained as player data

Fingerings chained from Table III's closed and open tones for each hole: inferred, not printed, from C4 to C5 and on the page notes. Where the table prints two rows for a note, the scale takes one and says which; the octave aids, holes 1, 2 and 5, aren't printed and are closed, except that hole 2 is open as the octave vent on the Ab5 and G5 pages

A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17) on the reed-performance pages; the Db4 and D4 pages, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, close the reed on a penalty contact at zero opening instead (56 kN/m, exponent 2, loss factor 8.82)

Quasi-steady orifice loss at the first open tone hole (all eleven on the D5 page, `open_hole_orifice 11`, all five on the F4 page, `open_hole_orifice 5`, and all nine on the Ab5 page, `open_hole_orifice 9`, commit 43ad828c9; all three on the earlier D4 page, `open_hole_orifice 3`, commit 043f9b8e9, and on the D4 page now as `dg_terminal_orifice 0.61` on its three open chimneys of the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, with the same C_vc): a pressure drop K |U| U with K = rho / (2 C_vc^2 A_h^2), C_vc = 0.61 (c_d 2.69, the free-streamline bound for a sharp edge) and no threshold velocity; on those four pages the holes are solved together through the bore, each hole's coefficient reading the gas at that hole on the continuous field of those cards, with two stated approximations: each orifice sees its own uncoupled radiation load, not the coupled one of the interaction row, and the sound the holes radiate still comes from the linear network, as for the first hole alone (the fully coupled orifice network is not built); no open hole beyond those has one

Staple pressure recovery of the double reed (Almeida, Vergez and Caussé 2007, eqs. 14-17; commit b57b46619), on the D4 and D5 pages: the blade is driven by the pressure drop across the opening and the bore input is raised by C_P (1/2) rho (q/S_c)^2, with C_P 0.8 and S_c 4e-6 m^2, one measured oboe reed's numbers (Figs 14 and 15), borrowed, not this reed's. S_c = 4 mm^2 is corroborated: the mold of Almeida, Vergez and Causse 2007 (Fig. 14) reads 4.2 mm^2 at the constriction (28.5 mm), and staple catalogue ovals (Chiarugi 2+ M 2.50 x 2.00 mm = 3.9 mm^2; Chiarugi 47-2 2.4 x 1.9 mm = 3.6 mm^2; Marigaux 1 2.40 x 1.80 mm = 3.4 mm^2; catalogue to 0.1 mm) span 3.4 to 4.2 mm^2 with it. C_P = 0.8 is the one free parameter of their Fig. 15 fit (the other quantities held), and the authors note that it matches an extrapolation of Azad 1996's data on turbulent flow in conical diffusers (half-angle 3.94 deg, Re 6.9e4; the staple's is 5.2 deg, L/d 20). The law neglects the viscous loss along the reed, as this card does

Bore air temperature and humidity profile along the bore on the D5, Db4, F4, Bb4, Ab5, G5 and D4 pages: the CLARINET pages' own continuous gas field, a borrowed shape and not an oboe's (no measured oboe bore profile is held): the exhaled-breath mixture (Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969) with the 14 stations of the bore air temperature Noreland (2013) measured in a clarinet, 304.15 K and water mole fraction 0.0442 at the barrel to 294.96 K and 0.0257 at the end of the clarinet's 0.655 m bore, only the positions rescaled by 0.634/0.655; it is on the oboe cards because the interaction and printed-length rows below run only on a continuous gas field, and a measured shape is the least invented one held

Mutual radiation impedance between the open holes and the bell on the D5, F4, Bb4, Ab5 and G5 pages (the Db4 and D4 pages have the computed mutual radiation of their discontinuous-Galerkin bore instead) (TMMI, Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard 2013, half-space factor 2), distances along the bore axis only, an upper bound for holes on opposite sides, never less than the sum of the two radii, so Bb4's doubled hole (holes 8 and 9 at one station) is coupled at its touching distance, 4.2 mm (commit 418a8f86b)

Printed thick-wall tone-hole lengths of Lefebvre and Scavone (2012) on the D5, F4, Bb4, Ab5, G5 and D4 pages (on the D4 page they are the lengths of the chimneys of its discontinuous-Galerkin bore; not on Db4, whose discontinuous-Galerkin bore has no row for them), in place of the engine's inner length

Vena contracta of the reed jet on the D5, Db4, F4, Bb4, Ab5 and G5 pages (the opt-in `contraction` row, commit 25b9bc64c; the contraction term of fs-phs GapFlowLaw without its channel terms, the staple law, where there is one, taken on the jet area; on Db4, F4, Bb4 and Ab5 the card has no staple row; it is not on D4, where it silences the note): C_c 0.611 = pi/(pi+2), the two-dimensional free-streamline bound, borrowed and a bound trial, not a measured coefficient of a double reed; the card's reed area is Almeida's printed typical rest area (about 2 mm^2), not their fitted 3.05 to 3.37 mm^2, so print does not say it already holds a contraction

Discontinuous-Galerkin bore on the Db4 page (degree 3, 51 elements, viscothermal wall memory with up to 60 poles per wall point from 50 Hz to 20 kHz at wall quadrature 4, the twenty tone-hole chimneys as ducts with their own states, a sparse Krylov propagator held to 1e-11 on the full state with a DOF cap of 32768), observed by the baffled receiver to 9.6 kHz, the reed as one lumped mode with the same six numbers closing on a penalty contact, and the bell and open holes radiating as one computed baffled-piston array with every mutual term; it replaces the transfer-matrix route on that page and carries neither the printed hole lengths nor the first-hole orifice; the earlier 9.6 kHz bore of that page (degree 2, 48 poles, cap 20480, quadrature 3) was not converged, and which of the four settings that differ moved the band energy was not isolated. The D4 page has the same bore at a 14 kHz band (`51 3 60 50 14000 0.01 1e-11 32768 4`), replacing the transfer-matrix route there as well; unlike Db4 it carries the staple row, the printed chimney lengths, `dg_terminal_orifice 0.61` on its three open chimneys and the printed series length t_a as a bore shortening (0.634 to 0.627618 m, commit 2756926e7)

Tongue contact on the reed tip on the Bb4, F4, D5 and Ab5 pages, not on D4 since its move to the discontinuous-Galerkin bore (the opt-in `tongue_contact` row, commit d986948c3; Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2009, Eq. 6, the fundamental clamped-free cantilever mode's projection of a uniform strip at the tip): strip 1.12e-5 m^2 (2 mm by this reed's 5.6 mm; the 2 mm is Li 2016's clarinet contact length), effective area 6.979e-5 m^2 (this reed's own face, k h0 / pM, not borrowed), force 0.2 N and release over 5 ms (Almeida 2017, a clarinet), held until 0.1845 s (the blow's 0.15 s start plus 34.5 ms, the alto saxophone tonguing contact time of Hofmann 2012); every number but the effective area is borrowed and no oboe tongue is printed; the reed-opening trace was not read

Measured reed lay on the F4 page (the four optional lay fields of the `reed` row): stiffness 5.7437e6 = Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012 Table 1's printed clarinet contact stiffness per area, 8.23e10, times this reed's own face k h0 / pM = 6.979e-5 m^2; exponent 2.0, onset opening 1.6e-4 m (45 % of this reed's rest opening) and Hunt-Crossley loss 0.0 s/m are the clarinet pages' values, borrowed; no oboe lay is printed; it ties the count on F4 and lowers it on Bb4 and D5, so it is on F4 only; it lifts the pitch 9 to 28 c

Room air at the bell and holes on the Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and G5 pages (the D4 page's discontinuous-Galerkin card has the same dry room air as `dg_exterior 293.15 101325 0` and reads it at 0.5 m on axis to 9.6 kHz): dry room air (relative humidity 0) at 293.15 K and 101325 Pa, the card row `exterior 293.15 101325 0`, the same row as the clarinet pages; the baffled outlet receiver (`baffled_outlet 0 0 0.5 32 128 4800`) reads that gas on the axis at 0.5 m, with 32 rings and 128 points to 4800 Hz

ISO 9613 air absorption on the path from the bell and holes to the receiver on the Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and G5 pages (not on the D4 page since its move to the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, whose card has no `observer_law` row): the card row `observer_law iso9613`, on dry room air (relative humidity 0), the same row as the clarinet pages; at 0.5 m its whole-band deviation from the classical law is 0.0025 dB (tolerance 1.0 dB), so it moves nothing audible at this range

Reed-outlet observer replays on time on the Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and G5 pages and the earlier D4 page: the outlet kernels keep their pre-arrival spread ahead of the arrival and the replay gate refuses an audible replay after the breath-off (an engine fix, commits 69b3011d6 and 8f0297fe2 of 2026-11-03, not a card row; it is in the ancestry of every oboe build); read on the K10 clips of those six pages, the sound falls 60 dB within 0.15 s of the release at 2.45 s and then to exact zero, with no rise in any 25 ms window

Octave vent (hole 2) of the G5 and Ab5 pages, re-specified to a bore of 0.81 mm (radius 0.405 mm) and a height of 0.7 mm: the bore range 0.66 to 0.81 mm is the patent's print (US 6,124,537); the depth 0.7 mm and the ranges 0.5 to 0.7 mm (bore) and 0.25 to 0.7 mm (depth) stand on the repo's citation of S. Fox's maker's page only, which could not be retrieved; the old 6 mm height was an assumption copied from hole 3 and the old 0.3 mm bore is Table III's printed, doubtful value; the point was declared before the renders and all three corners of the sourced range reach the written octave (790.9 to 792.6 Hz), and the same point on Ab5 removes the period doubling (817.20 Hz period-doubled with the old vent, 819.53 Hz a single series with it); hole 2 is the thumb-key vent by position only
physics_missing: a measured bore profile and bell flare: only reads from the paper's graphs exist
pad and key heights, undercut geometry and a full fingering chart

a double-reed valve driving this bore at the bands the oboe needs. The typed reed record, the jet contraction row and the constriction_noise row drive the discontinuous-Galerkin bore through the sparse Krylov propagator (the dense propagator's 2048-DOF cap no longer refuses the bore; the sparse cap is 32768 DOF), and the full Db4 at the 4.8 kHz design band renders steady at -3.0 cents. Not in yet: the open-hole orifice and the printed tone-hole lengths are not on the DG route (the live route has both), and nothing above 20 kHz is resolved by the bore (the receiver observes to 9.6 kHz). The open holes' mutual radiation is in the DG radiation operator (a computed baffled-piston array, every self and mutual term), not a row. The staple pressure recovery is an opt-in row on the typed reed: on the DG bore a D4 pilot pair at 6178 Pa speaks with it (0.85 Pa) and is silent without it (0.0017 Pa), no page yet. At the 9.6 kHz design band (degree 2, 48 wall-loss poles) the full Db4 was the Db4 page: 7 of 14 against the transfer-matrix page's 6 on the loose ruler and 4 against its 6 on the strict one, with the pitch 7.4 c sharp of the recording, the centroid 744 Hz against 1173 Hz and the harmonics-to-noise 63.4 dB against the recording's 40.4 (too clean), and without the printed hole lengths and the first-hole orifice the transfer-matrix page carried. At 20 kHz (degree 3) the bore was refused by a propagator certificate (residual 1.1361e-11 against the card's 1e-11), and the refusing propagator was not the main bore's: it was the stiff chimneys' dense series propagator, whose certificate is now evaluated in double-double with the f64 rounding counted (commit 67c1cf165; the tolerance was not loosened); the full Db4 renders on that converged bore (degree 3, 60 poles, quadrature 4, cap 32768) and is the Db4 page: 6 of 14, strict 4, the same note, with 7 to 8 dB more energy from 1.5 to 9.6 kHz than the 9.6 kHz bore. The flow-noise row's source (above 8 kHz at this blow) lies above the 4.8 kHz and 9.6 kHz DG bands, so those renders add no audible noise and their harmonics-to-noise stays too clean (70.6 dB at 4.8 kHz, 63.4 dB at 9.6 kHz, against the recording's 40.4); on the 20 kHz bore, observed to 9.6 kHz, it reads 56.5 dB, and whether the noise row, now inside the bore's band, changes the clip below 9.6 kHz was not measured

staple and reed channel geometry (the pressure recovery law is in, with one measured reed's two numbers borrowed; this reed's staple is not measured; The first 65 mm (staple and reed) are Table II's two printed radii, 0.87 mm at 33 mm and 2.4 mm at 91 mm from the apex, joined as a straight round cone, with a 7 mm cylinder at the tip that is assumed; the card's 0.539 cm^3 lies within 2 to 12 % of the volume Nederveen and de Bruijn measured for this specimen's staple and reed with an injection needle, 0.55 to 0.61 cm^3. No step is measured on this specimen, so the shape between the two printed radii is taken as a straight cone. A trial with the mold-measured channel of ONE other oboe reed (Almeida, Vergez and Causse 2007, Fig. 14, read by image: area +-0.2 mm^2, axial +-0.13 mm, one source, maker not stated; 0.43 cm^3 in the first 65 mm, with a step from 6.6 to 4.3 mm^2 between 27.65 and 27.9 mm that depends on that reed's blade length; the oval modelled round) in place of the cone, with nothing else changed, played flatter by 26.8, 6.7 and 11.7 c on the Bb4, F4 and D5 reed-performance cards and moved the grader's loose counts from 6 to 6, 6 to 6 and 6 to 5 (strict 5 to 4, 6 to 6, 5 to 4; on D5 the pitch gap to the recording grew from 12.5 to 24.2 c and left both rulers). It was not adopted: that reed is another, smaller specimen.  the jet contraction row is in, commit 25b9bc64c, with 0.611 borrowed as a bound, since no double reed's contraction is printed, and the channel's unsteady inertance is not in it, since no printed effective length of the channel is held)
a modern specimen: the only complete table is from 1967

A printed pressure for every note: Fuks and Sundberg print one for D4, F4, Bb4, D5 and F5 only, as a range (Table A6, two players, four dynamics, up and down); the pages use the second oboist's ff, rising. F4 (6865 Pa) plays in the first register, with or without the contraction row, and D5 (8041 Pa) speaks; Bb4 at 7551 Pa scored 5 of 15 against 6 and was not posted; D4 at 6178 Pa does not speak without the staple row and speaks with it (with the contraction row added to the staple, profile, interaction and length rows it is silent again); F5 has no printed fingering. G5 and Ab5 are blown at 10.689 kPa (109 cm H2O) and 10.983 kPa (112 cm H2O). Table A6 prints neither note: both values are the linear semitone interpolation between the second oboist's ff, rising-arpeggio F5 (103 cm H2O) and Bb5 (118 cm H2O), 3 cm H2O per semitone, the method used for the A4 value of the description (1 cm H2O = 98.0665 Pa). Every other note uses the pages' 7.4 kPa

The scale's tuning. Before the reed's closure stop the scale was flat because the reed passed through its lay; with it the notes sit -7 to +33 c from equal temperament, F4 plays an octave up in the second register (nothing was done to bring it back), and Bb4 sounds as B4. The reed's blade mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed: they need the authors or a measured reed

Nonlinear loss at the other open holes (none left on D5, F4, Ab5 and D4, where every open hole carries it; beyond the first on the rest), and a printed coefficient for the first: c_d 2.69 is the code's free-streamline bound, not a printed value (printed: 2 for a tube end, 13/9 for a flanged end and 1.18 for a sharp hole in PVC, the last through a secondary source), and this model's hole edges aren't printed. On Bb4 the second open hole sits at the first one's station and carries the same flow, and the third about 0.6 of it, at the played note (the engine's small-signal transfer, not a render)

An oboe's own bore air temperature profile (the D5, Db4, F4, Bb4, Ab5, G5 and D4 pages borrow a clarinet's), the holes' azimuths (the interaction takes axial distances only), and the spacing of Bb4's doubled hole (holes 8 and 9 at one axial station): the engine couples them at the touching distance, 4.2 mm, an upper bound, because their azimuths are not printed. On D5 the three together moved the steady tone about 11 c and the level under 1 dB against the same card with a constant field, and the grader's count by one measure when the staple row was absent; with the staple row the count is the same as without them

An oboe tongue's own area, force and contact time: the tongue row borrows the clarinet's 2 mm strip length, 0.2 N and 5 ms release and the alto saxophone's 34.5 ms contact time, and sets the strip width to this reed's 5.6 mm and the effective area to this reed's own face; whether the tongue closes the reed was not read (the 0.2 N is below the 1.24 N its stiffness takes at its opening)

An oboe reed's own lay (contact law between the reed and its lay): the F4 page borrows the clarinet's exponent, onset opening and loss and scales the clarinet's printed contact stiffness per area by this reed's face; the other pages keep the default slit lay, because the lay lowered their counts and lifted the pitch

Which key opens which octave vent, and the vent's own numbers: the Woodwind Fingering Guide's chart puts G5 and Ab5 on the first (thumb) octave key, but Table III's overblowing aids, holes 1, 2 and 5 (73, 129 and 182 mm), carry no key and hole 2 is chosen by position; the vent bore and depth are a patent's printed bore range and a maker's page cited by the repo, not this specimen's (Table III prints 0.3 mm for holes 1 and 2, doubtful, and no chimney length)
blocked: The paper's bore graphs are read and its tables were transcribed from the page images, but no open source prints an oboe reed's blade mass, stiffness or damping. Needs those from the authors or a measured reed, and a newer measured oboe.
